James Brown, by contrast, knew Patrick only as an adult Pennsylvanian; he could not have witnessed a birth in Ireland that occurred before he knew the Flynn family. His testimony about that event rests entirely on hearsay or assumption. A father with direct knowledge outweighs a son-in-law reporting from memory and inference about events he never witnessed.
